Now I wonder about the read rate of a floppy. Wikipedia alleges that the maximum rate of bits passin under the head was 1Mbps. 3711 floppies is a little over 5GiB. It would take more than 11 hours to read the data from all of them not counting the time it takes to change disks.

PC floppy drives were 360 RPM because up until DOS 5, the DOS disk I/O was timing dependent and wouldn't work with a higher spin rate. You could get duplicator grade drives, which would work fine with Windows. But I think the MFM interface was also limited to 1Mbps, so they would have to be USB or something.

Mac / Apple //gs drives were programmable speed, and by default went faster on inner tracks and slower on outer tracks to squeeze more data onto tracks with larger radius. Unfortunately, since most of the world was using PCs, floppy manufacturers started making the disks themselves crappier, and the media would stretch from the centripetal force from the higher spin rate of the apple drives.
